prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

| Term | Meaning |
| - | - |
| DepositPreauth entry | A ledger entry letting one account accept payments from a named sender, or any holder of a named credential set. |
| `Authorize` / `Unauthorize` | The fields that create and remove a sender-based grant. Exactly one of the four grant fields may be present. |
| `fixDepositPreauthSelf` | The amendment added here. Gates both behavioural changes. |
| `credentials::makeSorted` | Canonicalises a credential array. It reports duplicates by returning an **empty** set, not an error. |
| `tem` / `tec` / `tef` | `tem` rejects locally: never relayed, no fee. `tec` applies it and claims the fee. `tef` is a node-local fault. |

Three changes to the DepositPreauth transactor:

1. `Unauthorize` naming the sender is rejected in preflight rather than in preclaim.
2. The duplicate-credential sentinel from `makeSorted` is tested before use on the `UnauthorizeCredentials` path.
3. The transactor's two invariant hooks are implemented.

Tests are in the second commit, so the code and its coverage land together.

## Context of Change

**Item 1 is a policy change, not a conformance fix.** XLS-0070 §7.2 enumerates this transaction's failure conditions, and self-targeting is not among them. xrpl.org documents `temCANNOT_PREAUTH_SELF` as applying to the `Authorize` field specifically, and `tecNO_ENTRY` as "tried to revoke a preauthorization that does not exist in the ledger" — which a self-unauthorize always is, because the matching entry can never be created: `Authorize` naming the sender has been rejected since the DepositPreauth amendment shipped in 2018. The current code is therefore conformant and returns the accurate code. What this change buys is that a transaction which cannot succeed is refused before relay and before a fee is claimed. If that is not judged worth an amendment, items 2 and 3 do not depend on it.

The spec backs the other two. §7.2 lists duplicate and empty credential arrays as failure conditions without naming codes, so the choice of code is the implementation's, and `temMALFORMED` fits bad input better than the `tefINTERNAL` it replaces. §7.3 states the entry "will store a sorted list of credentials", the authority for item 3's sortedness assertion.

**Three claims that prompted this work did not survive checking; recorded so they are not re-raised.** The self-target asymmetry was called a defect — per §7.2 it is not, hence item 1 as policy. The duplicate-credential path was called reachable node corruption — it is neither, since `credentials::checkArray` rejects duplicates before preclaim runs, so `tefINTERNAL` was mis-classified rather than live. An invariant asserting the owner-count delta matches the object delta was proposed and is **wrong**: `increaseOwnerCount` resolves a sponsor and routes the delta to it, so it would misfire on every reserve-sponsored grant. It is deliberately absent, and a sponsored-create test here pins that down.

**The invariant hooks are live.** [`Transactor::operator()()` calls `checkInvariants(result, fee, InvariantScope::Full)`](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/d5bfe94f15ece0ba1b6c00004ee5b3f90383f2ab/src/libxrpl/tx/Transactor.cpp#L1640), which routes through `TxInvariantCheck` to this transactor's hooks, so a false return produces `tecINVARIANT_FAILED` on a transaction that would otherwise succeed. That is why item 3 is amendment-gated as well.

**Why it is safe.** Both behavioural changes are gated on `fixDepositPreauthSelf`: item 1's pre-amendment half is the unchanged `Authorize` test, and `finalizeInvariants` returns true immediately when the amendment is off. On a ledger without it every input produces today's result, and item 2 is unreachable per the `checkArray` ordering above. No consensus divergence.

## API Impact

- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)

`DepositPreauth` gains four private members that accumulate invariant state, changing its layout.

## Before / After

| Input | Before | After, amendment off | After, amendment on |
| - | - | - | - |
| `Authorize` == sender | `temCANNOT_PREAUTH_SELF` | unchanged | unchanged |
| `Unauthorize` == sender | `tecNO_ENTRY` | unchanged | `temCANNOT_PREAUTH_SELF` |

The hooks assert three properties of a touched grant: its `sfAccount` is the submitting account, at most one grant changes per transaction, and a created entry's `sfAuthorizeCredentials` is canonically sorted and so duplicate-free. Coverage exclusion covers only the violation branches, which cannot fire unless a write path above is broken.

## Test Plan

Cases added to `xrpl.app.DepositPreauth` cover self-target in both directions, duplicate and empty credential arrays, a created array's sort order, the hooks on a normal create and remove, and a sponsored create. Each amendment-sensitive case runs under both rule sets, so dropping the gate fails here rather than on a network.

```
./xrpld --unittest=xrpl.app.DepositPreauth
```

## Future Tasks

- xrpl.org's `temCANNOT_PREAUTH_SELF` wording goes stale when the amendment activates; needs an `XRPLF/xrpl-dev-portal` PR.
- The amendment name suits item 1 but not items 2 and 3. Happy to rename before merge.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: This is a well-reasoned, amendment-gated hardening change to DepositPreauth. I traced the preflight self-target gating, the preclaim duplicate/empty-credential handling, and the new invariant hooks against the MR's own rationale and the accompanying tests, and did not find a confident correctness or security defect: the amendment gating correctly preserves pre-amendment behavior, the temMALFORMED changes are backed by tests that pin the exact codes, and the invariant counters reset naturally because a new transactor instance is constructed per transaction. The one thing worth a quick sanity check before merge is noted below — it's a maintainability observation, not a confirmed bug.

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body:
### 🔵 Needs a closer look It changes consensus-critical transaction processing behavior and introduces invariant enforcement behind a new amendment, which warrants final human review despite the added tests.
Pull request overview This PR hardens the `DepositPreauth` transactor by adding an amendment-gated policy change for self-targeted unauthorize, improving defensive handling around credential canonicalization, and implementing transaction-specific invariant hooks to catch unexpected write-path regressions. **Changes:** - Amendment-gated: reject `Unauthorize == sfAccount` in **preflight** (avoid relay + fee burn for a transaction that cannot succeed). - Defensive checks around credential canonicalization for `UnauthorizeCredentials` (handle the `makeSorted()` “empty means duplicates” sentinel before building a keylet). - Implement `DepositPreauth` transactor invariant hooks and add unit tests covering the new behaviors (including sponsorship).
File summaries | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | src/test/app/DepositAuth_test.cpp | Adds unit tests for self-unauthorize fee behavior (amendment on/off), duplicate unauthorize-credentials rejection, and invariant hook coverage (including sponsored reserve). | | src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/payment/DepositPreauth.cpp | Implements amendment-gated preflight behavior, defensive credential sorting checks in preclaim, and transactor invariant entry/finalize logic. | | include/xrpl/tx/transactors/payment/DepositPreauth.h | Adds per-transaction private members to accumulate invariant state (counts + flags). | | include/xrpl/protocol/detail/features.macro | Introduces the new `DepositPreauthSelf` fix amendment definition. |
Review details - **Files reviewed:** 4/4 changed files - **Comments generated:** 1 - **Review effort level:** Lite

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: `visitInvariantEntry` returns early when a DepositPreauth SLE is modified (before && !isDelete), which means the invariant counters/flags won’t reflect unexpected in-place edits to an existing ltDEPOSIT_PREAUTH object. Since the invariant is meant to guard against transactor write-path regressions, it should treat modifications as a touched grant too (at least for counting/owner checks).

prs.body:
The `lsfDepositAuth` flag (introduced by the `DepositAuth` amendment) limits the AccountIDs that can deposit into an account that has the flag set.  The original design only allowed deposits to complete if the account with the flag set also signed the transaction that caused the deposit.

The `DepositPreauth` (note the `Pre`) ledger type allows an account with the `lsfDepositAuth` flag set to preauthorize additional accounts.  A preauthorized account may also sign deposits that go into an account with the flag set.  An account can add `DepositPreauth` objects to the ledger (and remove them as well) using the `DepositPreauth` transaction.

The branch is separated into several logically independent commits which will be squashed together once the review is complete.

1. The first commit adds the new ledger type and the transactor that allows the ledger type to be added and removed from the ledger.
2. The second commit adds support to pre-existing RPC commands that need to handle the new ledger type.
3. The third commit adds a new `deposit_authorized` RPC command that was proposed in the spec.
4. The next three commits add support for preauthorization in Payments, Escrow, and PayChan.  These are the three kinds of transactions (other than Checks) that can have the effect of depositing into an account.  CheckCash transactions are unaffected because (as currently specified) they may only be signed by the Destination of the Check.
5. The last commit snags a few very small fixes that were attached to amendments that have been stalled (`FlowCross` and `Checks`).  I'm moderately confident that `DepositPreauth` will not get stalled, so this seems like a reasonable way to get these small fixes onto the network.

Reviewers: @seelabs for PayChan experience, @HowardHinnant for general code goodness.  Delighted to hear from anyone else as well.  Thanks.

reviewCommentsList.body:
Interesting.  `ApplyView::dirRemove()` returns a `bool`.  `dirDelete()` returns a `TER` which is either a `tefBAD_LEDGER` or a `tesSUCCESS`.  I'm in the transactor's `doApply()`, so I'd _prefer_ to return a `tec` code over a `tef`.  On the other hand, this should really only happen if the ledger is corrupt.  So returning a `tef` may be okay.  And it would keep me aligned with all the other places that call `dirDelete()`.

Would you prefer that I return a `tefBAD_LEDGER`, or a `tecINTERNAL` or a `tecFAILED_PROCESSING` if I'm unable to remove the directory entry?  Thanks.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: BTW, should I add a JIRA item to replace all occurrences of `dirAdd()` and `dirDelete()` with `ApplyView::dirInsert()` and `ApplyView::dirRemove()`?

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body:
I made a conscious decision to return a `bool` and not a `TER` since the result was very much binary and I didn't want to encourage multiple weird error codes. We're performing a conceptually simple operation: remove an entry from a page and that can either succeed or fail, so `bool` seemed like the right result. A failure in that code path would really be an exceptional circumstance anyways. What you return from a transactor in response to a failure is a good question. I'd be fine with continuing to return `tefBAD_LEDGER` but I can also get behind `tecFAILED_PROCESSING`.

Instead of a JIRA ticket, please create a GitHub Issue. Please be sure to note that `dirAdd` has two modes of operation, controlled by a `bool` argument: "insert" and "append" and they correspond to `ApplyView::dirInsert` and `ApplyView::dirAppend` respectively.

issues.title: [XLS-0096] DepositPreauth Checked in doApply Not preclaim
issues.author: hgandhi-rx
issues.body:
## Summary

[XLS-0096] DepositPreauth Checked in doApply Not preclaim.

## Details

**Title:** DepositPreauth Checked in doApply Instead of preclaim  

**File:Line:** `src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/token/ConfidentialMPTSend.cpp:208, 213-216`

**Description:**  
`verifyDepositPreauth()` is called inside `doApply()`, not `preclaim()`. Every other XRPL transactor honoring DepositAuth checks it in preclaim. The ZKP is verified in preclaim (expensive), then the fee is charged and the deposit-auth check fires in doApply — meaning a sender unaware that the destination has `lsfDepositAuth` pays both the ZKP computation (in preclaim) and the transaction fee for a transaction that was always going to fail.

**Additional issue:** Line 208 uses `view().peek()` (mutable access) for the destination account SLE, which is only needed for `verifyDepositPreauth` — a read-only operation. Using `peek()` unnecessarily marks the SLE dirty.

**Fix:** Move `verifyDepositPreauth` to `preclaim()`. Change `view().peek(keylet::account(destination))` to `view().read(keylet::account(destination))`.

## Impact

Branch: [`ripple/attackathon-april-2026`](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/tree/ripple/attackathon-april-2026)

issues.title: DepositPreauth prevents Trustline deletion
issues.author: RichardAH
issues.body:
## Issue Description

In the following scenario a Trustline becomes undeletable:
1. A user makes a trustline to an issuer
2. The issuer sends some tokens to the user.
3. The issuer has enabled DepositPreauth flag
4. The user wants to return the tokens (and thus set their side of the ripple state object to default state).

This should always be allowed, users should not be obligated to hold tokens they no longer wish to hold.
Currently the DepositPreauth logic does not test for this.
